newsitem.title: JAPAN: Profits at Toyota units jump, good year seen.
newsitem.headline: Profits at Toyota units jump, good year seen.

text.p: Most Toyota Motor Corp affiliates enjoyed big increases in their first-half profits, helped by a recovery in the parent firm's production, and now see better full-year profits ahead, the companies announced on Tuesday.
Component maker Denso Corp said it had boosted its parent current profit to 46.63 billion yen ($409 million) in the half year to September 30, up more than 62 percent on the previous year.

"Higher profits and sales were due to increased component sales to Toyota and higher sales of our new business such as cell phones," said a spokesman for the firm, which is 23 percent owned by Toyota.
The company forecast a full-year profit of 98 billion yen ($859 million), up more than 40 percent on last year.
Current profit is pretax and includes gains or losses on non-operating activities such as investment in stocks.
Toyoda Automatic Loom Works Ltd, which carries out some of Toyota's vehicle production, said it boosted its interim parent earnings by 88 percent to 14.32 billion yen ($125 million).
It forecast a 28.50 billion yen ($250 million) parent current profit for the full year, up more than 36 percent.
"Strong domestic demand for Toyota cars contributed to our bigger profit," a spokesman said.
The firm, which is owned 23 percent by Toyota, produced 125,000 Toyota-designed vehicles in the first half, up from an initially planned 102,000, and against 75,000 a year earlier.
Toyota's overall first-half domestic vehicle output rose 6.2 percent from a year earlier to 1.62 million units, after a 12.7 percent fall in the same period last year.
Its vehicle exports rose 17 percent to 664,145 units in the same period, while its domestic sales stood at 957,526, little changed from the year before.

Three other Toyota affiliates -- trading arm Toyota Tsusho Corp, component maker Aisin Seiki Co Ltd and machinery maker Toyoda Machine Works Ltd -- posted better interim profits and revised up their forecasts for the full year.
Toyota Auto Body Co Ltd, which makes small vans, said it managed a slightly better interim result, but failed to achieve its May interim forecast.
However, it said it expects to achieve its full-year parent current profit forecast of 6 billion yen ($52.6 million), helped by the introduction of new models in the second half. ($1=114)
